Now the functional proof — reload the dev page, load the catalog, simulate a quiet apply, and confirm the catalog forgets and the card still resolves after refetch:

The core fix is proven — `flat` is null after a quiet apply. But the card didn't appear afterward; let me probe why before concluding anything:

End-to-end proof: poisoned the in-memory intro, ran a quiet apply, and the very next long-press refetched and spoke the new placeholder text. Now the toggle proof and ship:

Deploy completed but the version check hit a 502 — likely the server mid-restart after kickstart. Retrying:

Fixed and live as **build 168**. The tooltip wasn't cached wrongly on disk — it was stale in memory, and here's the mechanism:

**Root cause:** the tooltip fix (build 167) changed only data files, so it travelled as a **quiet apply** — the delta feature stamps the new build and evicts changed files but deliberately skips the reload. Meanwhile `feature_Chooser.load()` reads `features/tree.json` once per page and holds the catalog in memory. So your phone had the fresh file on disk and the panel said 167, but every long-press card kept answering from the catalog the page had read before the update. The wasm `patch` path shares the same no-reload ending, so it had the same latent hole.

**The fix:** a new subfeature node, `chooser/fresh-catalog`, wraps `feature_Delta.quiet` and makes the chooser forget its held catalog before anything re-renders — the next reader refetches the build the device is actually running. Proven in headless Chrome end-to-end: I poisoned the in-memory intro, ran a quiet apply, and the very next long-press showed the new placeholder text. Toggle proven both ways.

**For your phone right now:** build 168 carries new code, so it arrives as a normal apply with a reload — accepting it clears the stale memory and the 👤 tooltip will read correctly. From here on, silent updates refresh the catalog too, so this class of staleness is gone.

### p6a
*2026-08-15 21:50*

> no it works now

Fixing a typo I just introduced in that spec line:

Toggle proven both ways. Committing and deploying:

Shipped — **build 169 is live**, and the stamp is being served from the mini's bake.

**What you asked for is now a node: `serve/features/auto-export`** — *"the bake checks its sources; the catalog checks its bake."* Two halves:

- **Server**: any request under `features/` first compares the newest mtime anywhere in the source `features/` tree against the baked `tree.json`. Sources newer → the exporter re-runs before the request is answered (~4.5s, paid once per edit; embeddings follow detached). On the mini the sources are absent by design, so the check is a no-op and the deploy's bake stays the truth — a release remains a committed state.
- **Device**: the export now writes a `stamp` beside the bake (a content hash of tree.json). The chooser's held catalog revalidates against that tiny file on every read — a full refetch only when the words actually moved. So an edit reaches a phone's tooltip on its next look, no reload, no update-apply, no redeploy needed on the dev machine.

Proven end to end before shipping: edit a node's `.md` → the dev server's next `tree.json` carries the new words and the stamp moves; revert → the stamp round-trips to its exact old value; and in the browser, a catalog already held in memory picked up an on-disk edit on its next read — which you saw working live yourself. Toggle proven both ways (the `.rs` leaves the emitted crate, the `.js` leaves the site).

Two named risks in the spec, both dev-only and self-healing: concurrent requests can race the same re-export (a reader in the rewrite window can catch a 404), and because the re-export runs inside whichever request noticed first, a concurrent read can pair a mid-export tree with a mismatched stamp — the held-vs-served comparison then heals it one read later. That pairing race is exactly what my first scripted card-test tripped over before converging.

One debugging find worth keeping: route paths arrive **slash-stripped** (`clean_path`) — my first predicate matched `/features` and silently never fired. The spec records the convention.
